class.name: FenceGuidePost4D
class.brief_description: A movable corner of a [FenceGenerator4D]'s footprint.
class.description: FenceGuidePost4D marks one corner of a fence's footprint, for the [constant FenceGenerator4D.INPUT_SHAPE_RADIAL_POST_NODES] shape. It must be a direct child of a [FenceGenerator4D], which uses the positions of all of its guide post children as the fence's corners, and regenerates the fence whenever a guide post is moved, added, or removed, at the end of the frame and on a worker thread, see [method FenceGenerator4D.queue_update_fence_mesh]. The position is where the post meets the ground. Only the position matters: a guide post is a point, so its rotation and scale are reset to identity whenever they change. The generator gives each guide post the mesh of the post standing at its position, so the guide post is visible and can be clicked to select it. That mesh is regenerated by the parent and does not need to be edited, and like the fence's own mesh it is only saved with the scene while the parent's [member FenceGenerator4D.update_automatically] is disabled. A degenerate guide post adds no corner to the fence, gets no mesh, and shows a configuration warning. Since the corners are projected onto a sphere around the generator's origin before their convex hull is taken, see [method FenceGenerator4D.build_seed_mesh_from_corners], every other placement is a corner: the degenerate ones are a guide post at the origin, which is where a newly added one starts, one in the same direction from the origin as an earlier guide post, and one at the same position as an earlier guide post. [b]Note:[/b] Guide posts are saved with the scene and work at runtime, but a node per corner costs more than the corners stored as data, so exported projects warn about them. Before shipping, switch the generator to [constant FenceGenerator4D.INPUT_SHAPE_RADIAL_POINTS], which keeps the corners and removes the posts.
